analysis.title: Marketcolour + HF Update / GS Macro Outlooks / SCA Dg / RHM Cut / B&M
key_insights: US equities closed the week lower on a tougher risk backdrop: VIX at 20, 10-year yield at 5.13%, USD breaking out and oil above $90. SPX fell 40bps to 7561, NDX fell 91bps to 25136 and RTY fell 31bps to 2790.
SPX sector breadth was 8 of 11 sectors higher on Friday. Staples rose 122bps and Energy rose 116bps, while Tech fell 172bps.

NDX broke a four-week losing streak, with semis up 8% on the week, but it is still below its 200-day moving average. NVDA lost about $500bn of market cap while AMD and AVGO together added about $500bn or more.
Semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 30% since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002. GS's AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P.
Net selling in US Financials last week was the largest in 8 months, at the 99th percentile of the past 5 years.
In Europe, EU Big Oils rose 1.9% and outperformed, while EU Luxury fell 60bps after Richemont's numbers (Richemont -3.8%).

Fundamental L/S hedge funds rose 1.1% last week with alpha of -0.3%. Alpha losses came from China equities and Health Care, partly offset by asset selection, crowded longs and short concentration. YTD they are up 9.7% with alpha of +7.1%.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by single-stock short sales and partly offset by short covering and long buying in macro products. US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile one-year) and net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile one-year).

The GS cash desk saw persistent NVDA supply from the long-only community, with money rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. The desk says appetite to re-engage with semis still looks limited despite NDX ending its losing streak.
CTA positioning in NDX is back near maximum short levels.

This week's catalysts are NVDA earnings Tuesday (first report under interim CEO Colette Kress) and BABA Thursday. Consumer prints include TSN and ARMK Monday, HD Tuesday, TJX, TGT and LOW Wednesday, WMT, ROST and GAP Thursday, and BJ Friday. Macro focus is US Retail Sales Tuesday and FOMC minutes Wednesday.

GS downgraded SCA to Sell as a high conviction call. Estimates are about 10% below the Street and the call implies 16% downside to the price target. It rests on the team's global pulp supply and demand work and on industry events such as London Pulp Week.

GS cut Rheinmetall forecasts after Q3 results and a fireside chat with the CEO, ahead of cuts likely at the upcoming capital markets day. The largest percentage cuts are in Weapons & Ammo, where growth momentum has deteriorated. 2030 EBIT falls 25% and 2030 EPS falls 30% to about 104, and the shares trade on under 8x 2030e P/E.

GS raised its B&M price target to 345p from 220p on Neutral. FY27E/FY28E like-for-like growth assumptions rise to +2.3%/+3% from +0.7%/+1%, gross margin assumptions rise +100bp/+30bp from flat, and FY27E/28E PBT rises 6%/15% to £310mn/£344mn.
Dom Wilson outlines 10 market themes for 2027, including a maturing cycle, an AI impulse peaking and bonds reclaiming macro and hedging value.
